answer: I'd like to talk about a book that I finished a few weeks ago and still find myself thinking about. A book I recently read and thoroughly enjoyed was a work of non-fiction about human psychology and decision-making. It was about the [[mental shortcuts]] we all take, and the way our emotions and habits push us towards choices that are not always logical. The book explained, in a remarkably accessible way, why people so often behave irrationally. A friend had recommended it, and I was immediately [[intrigued]] by the subject. Part of the reason I picked it up was my job, because at the education consultancy I watch students make huge decisions about their futures, sometimes for surprisingly emotional reasons, and I wanted to understand that better. What I found most [[compelling]] was how it used real experiments to illustrate its points, which made the ideas stick. I read it far more quickly than I expected, because it was genuinely [[gripping]] despite being educational. Most evenings I would sit down to read one chapter with a cup of tea and end up reading three. It completely changed how I think about my own choices and biases. Honestly, a good non-fiction book that leaves you seeing the world differently is a real treasure. Since finishing it, I have found myself noticing these psychological patterns in everyday life, even in the way I shop or argue with my sister. I think the best books are the ones that stay with you long after the final page, and this one certainly did. I have already recommended it to several friends, calling it one of the most [[enlightening]] books I have read in years.

followUps.q: Do you usually prefer fiction or non-fiction?
followUps.answer: These days I lean towards non-fiction, because I like learning something useful. That said, I still enjoy a good Bengali novel now and then, especially on long bus journeys or rainy monsoon afternoons.

followUps.q: Do you prefer printed books or e-books?
followUps.answer: Printed books, without a doubt. I like the feel of the pages and being able to [[scribble]] notes in the margins, although e-books are admittedly handy when I'm travelling.
